name: Los Angeles (city): Retail
law: Los Angeles Fair Work Week Ordinance

coverage.summary: Retail businesses (principal NAICS codes 44-45) with 300 or more employees globally, for employees who work at least 2 hours a week inside the City of Los Angeles.
coverage.employees: Retail employees who perform at least 2 hours of work in a workweek within the City of Los Angeles.
notes: Franchisee employees count toward the threshold only for retail franchises over 15,000 square feet (Office of Wage Standards FAQ).
The City Council voted in September 2026 to extend the ordinance to fast-food workers. Until that takes effect, only retail is covered here.

citation.quote: An Employer shall provide an Employee with a written work schedule at least 14 days before the start of the Work Period.

premiums.label: New shift, or shift moved without losing time, after the schedule was posted

citation.quote: One additional hour of pay at the regular rate for each change to the date, time or location of a shift that results in no loss of time, or that adds more than 15 minutes of work time.

premiums.label: More than 15 minutes added to a shift after the schedule was posted

citation.quote: One additional hour of pay at the regular rate for each change that adds more than 15 minutes of work time.

premiums.label: Time cut (15 minutes or more) or shift cancelled after the schedule was posted

citation.quote: Half of the regular rate for the scheduled time not worked when the employer cuts scheduled work time by at least 15 minutes or cancels a shift.

An Employer shall not schedule an Employee to work a Shift that starts less than ten hours from the Employee's last Shift without the Employee's written consent. An Employer shall pay an Employee a premium of time and a half for each Shift not separated by at least ten hours.

exceptions.label: I accepted a voluntary change to cover an absence
exceptions.description: The employee accepted an employer-initiated change caused by another employee's absence, after being told that acceptance was voluntary and could be declined.

exceptions.label: I accepted extra hours offered to current staff
exceptions.description: The employee accepted additional hours offered to existing employees before new hiring, under LAMC § 185.05.

exceptions.label: The added hours were paid as overtime
exceptions.description: Additional hours that require an overtime premium under California Labor Code § 510.

otherRights.label: Right to decline hours, shifts or locations not on your posted schedule (consent must be in writing)
Extra hours must be offered to current employees before new hires

enforcement.agency: Los Angeles Office of Wage Standards

sources.title: LAMC Chapter XVIII, Article 5 (Fair Work Week)
Office of Wage Standards: Fair Work Week
Fair Work Week Rules and Regulations (May 2025)

notes: Notice is measured to 12:00 a.m. on the first day of the work schedule: a premium is owed for any change made after the schedule's 14-day posting deadline, whichever shift it affects.
The rest premium is time and a half on every hour of the second shift (OWS FAQ), minus hours already paid an overtime premium. Shiftowed shows the extra half-time.
Same-workday split shifts are not covered by the rest rule.
The Office of Wage Standards asks workers to give the employer a Notice to Cure before filing a complaint.
